review_note: Injectivity is characterized by Hom(-,I) exactness, all extensions 0→I→A→B→0 splitting, and Ext(B,I)=0. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $I$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The object $I$ is injective.
\item The functor $B \mapsto \Hom_\mathcal{A}(B, I)$
is exact.
\item Any short exact sequence
$$
0 \to I \to A \to B \to 0
$$
in $\mathcal{A}$ is split.
\item We have $\Ext_\mathcal{A}(B, I) = 0$ for
all $B \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $I$ be an object of an abelian category.
conclusions: The four conditions—injectivity, exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$, splitness of every short exact sequence with left term $I$, and vanishing $\operatorname{Ext}(B,I)$ for all $B$—are equivalent.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-injectives}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $I$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The object $I$ is injective.
\item The functor $B \mapsto \Hom_\mathcal{A}(B, I)$
is exact.
\item Any short exact sequence
$$
0 \to I \to A \to B \to 0
$$
in $\mathcal{A}$ is split.
\item We have $\Ext_\mathcal{A}(B, I) = 0$ for
all $B \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: An existing product of injective objects in an abelian category remains injective; no infinite-product existence claim is made. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Suppose $I_\omega$, $\omega \in \Omega$ is a set of injective
objects of $\mathcal{A}$. If $\prod_{\omega \in \Omega} I_\omega$
exists then it is injective.
hypotheses: Let $(I_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ be a set-indexed family of injective objects in an abelian category; suppose their product exists.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-product-injectives}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Suppose $I_\omega$, $\omega \in \Omega$ is a set of injective
objects of $\mathcal{A}$. If $\prod_{\omega \in \Omega} I_\omega$
exists then it is injective.
